title: Track governance decisions through durable projection and application receipts
scope: relay-side stages only (signed -> relay-accepted -> projection-committed). The consumer-received and applied/rejected stages belong to agentbox and the mutation owner and are NOT implemented here.

findings_addressed.finding: handle_event sends OK and broadcasts after save_event, then projects
findings_addressed.assessment: The ordering is retained deliberately — NIP-01 requires the OK, and it is truthful about what it certifies (storage). What was missing is any record of what happened afterwards. A durable receipt is now written per signed event, so an OK is no longer the last word on a decision's fate.

findings_addressed.finding: Projection inserts decision and updates case separately
findings_addressed.root_cause: Two independent prepared statements, each with its result discarded, so a decision row could land while the case state update did not.
findings_addressed.fix: The decision INSERT, the case UPDATE and the receipt's transition to projection-committed are submitted as one D1 batch — a single implicit transaction. A half-applied projection is unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely.

governance_receipts table keyed by the FULL 64-hex signed event id, carrying stage (signed | relay-accepted | projection-committed | projection-failed), stage_error, and the full correlation set: request_event_id, case_id, signer_pubkey, decision_outcome, target_operation, supersedes_event_id, decision_id, signed_at, accepted_at, projected_at, replays.

findings_addressed.finding: Retrying the same signed event must not duplicate the mutation
findings_addressed.fix: The receipt row IS the durable replay record ADR-2010 permits where the storage boundary prevents spanning envelope and projection in one transaction. A replay of an already-committed event is counted and short-circuits before any write. A replay of a receipt still at relay-accepted or projection-failed is treated as reconciliation and retried; the retry is safe because the decision insert is INSERT OR IGNORE on a deterministic decision id and the case update is a state assignment, not an increment.

atomicity_position: End-to-end atomicity across save_event and the projection is NOT claimed and is not achievable on D1: save_event has already committed by the time a projection is planned. ADR-2010 explicitly permits the alternative — a durable replay record with idempotent reconciliation — and that is what is implemented. The projection itself is genuinely atomic.

derived_fields.applied: true only for projection-committed. The operator-facing distinction ADR-2010 turns on: a denied action and an approved action whose write failed must never look the same.
derived_fields.awaitsProjection: true where a further projection attempt is warranted (signed, relay-accepted, projection-failed).

api.authority_note: Scoped to the relay's existing administrative authority. ADR-2010's history-consumer extension leaves cross-case read authority for CP-04/05/08/09 to ratify, so no broader authority was invented here.

failure_injection: after save / before projection completes: commit_projection fails, asserting no decision row, no case state change, receipt at projection-failed with the reason retained, and is_applied() false
receipt store itself unavailable: reported as NotRecorded, never swallowed, no mutation
repeated failures: mutation never applies; a later success applies it exactly once
duplicate replay of a committed event: commit_projection is not called at all

remaining: No deployed D1 exercise. The batch's all-or-nothing semantics are modelled in the fake store, not observed against D1.

consumer-received and applied/rejected stages are not implemented — they belong to agentbox and the mutation owner, and require the versioned receipt contract ADR-2010 says forum and agentbox maintainers must agree.
project_appeal and project_supersession are NOT yet receipt-wired; only the first-order project_action_response path is.
Retention policy for governance_receipts is unset — rows accumulate.
Browser-side acceptance (rationale capture, signer cancellation, acknowledgement timeout, conflicting in-flight actions) is not covered by these tests.
Revoked-signer and conflicting-response cases are governed by the existing authority checks, not by the receipt layer; the receipt records what happened, it does not add an authority gate.
